attributes.action: Calls for stricter regulations for the shipping industry
attributes.additional_details:
The spread of plastic pellets (nurdles) into the River Tyne has caused uproar among local residents and charities with stark concerns about the incident's prolonged impact on the NE coastline. Calls are mounting for appropriate action, including mandatory measures at sea to prevent another disaster of this kind. 
We are therefore asking the Government to: 
A full investigation into the Port of Tyne collision 
Introduce stricter regulations for the shipping industry
attributes.background: Stricter nationwide regulations for the shipping industry following a ship colliding with a container ship at the Port of Tyne (South Shields) 19/07/26. It released 1 billion nurdles into the River Tyne. Nurdles cause death to marine and wildlife. This is the worst environmental disaster in the NE.

rejection.details:
We're not sure exactly how you would like to see shipping regulations strengthened. 

In addition, we cannot accept petitions which call for action on a local level. 

You could ask your MP to take action on your concerns about this issue, including by asking them to present a public (paper) petition about this.

You can find contact details for your local MP here: https://members.parliament.uk/FindYourMP

You could also raise your issue with a local councillor who represents you. You can use this page to find out who your local councillors are, and how to contact them: https://www.gov.uk/find-your-local-councillors

You may also wish to sign this petition which calls for a similar action: https://petition.parliament.uk/petitions/759563
